title: Collections and Disbursements in Tanzania: How to Collect and Send Payments at Scale
summary: Learn how businesses in Tanzania use Miden's Accrual and disbursement solutions to manage collections, Disbursements, reconciliation and high-volume payments.
body_markdown:
Tanzania's Collections and Disbursements economy has grown sharply over the past five years with businesses now processing money at an enormous scale, creating a new set of payment challenges.


According to Financial reports, Tanzania's mobile money market moved TZS 214.6 trillion across 4.08 billion transactions in In FY2021/22.


By 2026, that had grown to[TZS 640.2 trillion across 10.09 billion transactions](https://mawasiliano.go.tz/news/matumizi-ya-pesa-mtandao-yafikie-trilioni-640-2) — nearly triple the value and 2.5x the volume


For businesses, that growth creates a simple question:


How do you keep collections, payouts and reconciliation under control when customers and business partners are already moving money digitally at this scale?


This guide answers that question and more by explaining how companies can handle pay-ins and payouts at scale and which businesses offers the[best payment infrastructure.](https://www.miden.co/)


## How Do Collections and Disbursements work for Businesses in Tanzania?


A business payment solution is the infrastructure that helps a company receive payments, send funds and keep track of the movement of money.


On the incoming side, this includes **collections or pay-ins** .


On the outgoing side, it includes **payouts or disbursements** .


Generally, these flows involve mobile money, bank accounts, cards and other digital payment channels, but mobile money is central to Tanzania's payment market.


Businesses may need to accept payments through major mobile wallets, bank transfers, virtual card networks and online payment channels.


Tanzania has also invested in infrastructure to make these systems work better together.


In 2025, the number of financial service providers deploying Tanzania's national QR payment standard,[TANQR increased from 15 in 2024 to 27](https://thechanzo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/National-Payment-System-Report-2025.pdf#16#2) , including 21 banks and five mobile money operators, and one non-bank aggregator. A net addition of 12 institutions under one year.


### Tanzania Pay-ins and Pay-outs Use Cases & Rails in 2026


**Business Payment Solutions** **Use Case** **Description** **Common Tanzanian Payment Channels/Rails**


**Pay-In (Collections)** **Customer Payments** Retailers, travel businesses, e-commerce, and service providers receiving payments and identifying them quickly. Mobile Money (M-Pesa, Airtel Money, Mixx by Yas, Halopesa, T-Pesa) ; TANQR (Lipa Namba) ; Card Payments (Visa, Mastercard) ; Bank Transfers


**Invoice Collections** B2B companies needing to know when an invoice is paid without manual account checks. Bank Transfers (CRDB, NMB, etc.) ; TIPS (Business-to-Business payments) ; Payment Links (via card or mobile wallet)


**Marketplace Collections** Platforms receiving money from customers while tracking which merchant/service provider is entitled to each payment. Mobile Money ; TIPS (with Directory Service for merchant identification) ; TANQR ; Aggregator Platforms (e.g., Selcom Lipa, Malipopay)


**Subscription & Recurring** Digital businesses managing repeated customer payments without manual rebuilding each month. Mobile Money (recurring debit capabilities vary by provider) ; Card Payments (supports renewals) ; Request to Pay (TIPS feature)


**Pay-Out (Disbursements)** **Supplier Payments** Manufacturers, retailers, hospitality, and enterprises paying many suppliers as part of normal operations. Bank Transfers ; Mobile Money (to supplier wallets) ; TIPS (B2B)


**Agent & Field Payments** Companies with agents, drivers, contractors, or field teams sending funds to many recipients. Mobile Money (most practical for individual recipients) ; Agency Banking Networks (e.g., Selcom Huduma agents) ; Bank Transfers


**Marketplace Payouts** Platforms collecting from customers before settling merchants, drivers, hosts, or service providers. Mobile Money Wallets ; Bank Accounts ; TIPS (Business-to-Person disbursements via participating DFSPs)


**Customer Refunds** Digital businesses handling failed orders, cancellations, and refunds without manual finance tasks. Mobile Money (reversal to source wallet) ; Card Reversals (Visa/Mastercard support refunds) ; Bank Transfers


**Financial-Service Disbursements** Fintechs, lenders, and insurers sending loan funds, claims, or payments at high volume. Mobile Money (high-volume, low-value disbursements) ; Bank Transfers; TIPS (instant retail payments)


*Collated & Sourced from :[The Bank of Tanzania - National Payment Report 2025](https://thechanzo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/National-Payment-System-Report-2025.pdf)*


### Why Are Collections and Disbursements Becoming More Complex in Tanzania?


As transaction volumes surge and more businesses move online, the challenge has shifted from " *Can I receive money?* " to " *Can I see, track, and reconcile every shilling across multiple channels in real time?* "


This need compounds when a company operates across countries or currencies and has to manage payment providers, settlement schedules, liquidity, FX, transaction status, refunds and reconciliation at the same time.


Thus, Tanzania's collections and disbursements are becoming more complex not because payment rails are failing, but because success has changed what businesses expect from them. Some reasons include:


### The volume paradox: more money, more problems


In 2025 alone,[Tanzanians made 2.30 billion person-to-business digital payments](https://dailynews.co.tz/mobile-money-reshapes-economy/#go-to-tie-body) worth TZS 37.52 trillion. At the same time, the number of merchants accepting digital payments more than doubled to 2.79 million.


This growth is good news for financial inclusion. But it makes it difficult for businesses to find out which payment corresponds to which invoice.


As[Shomari Shija](https://www.itweb.co.za/article/making-payments-work-harder/mQwkoM6Y9lp73r9A) , Tanzanian fintech leader puts it; *"Businesses are no longer asking for faster payments; they are asking for smarter payments."*


### Fragmentation beneath the surface


TIPS (Tanzania Instant Payment System) was designed to solve interoperability, connecting banks and mobile money providers through a single real-time hub rather than bilateral integrations. But interoperability at the rail level does not automatically deliver clarity at the business level.


A business collecting payments today might initiate transactions through M-Pesa, a bank transfer, a card payment, and a TANQR scan in the same day, but receive funds at different times due to differences in settlements and reconciliation times.


For a small merchant, this is manageable. For a growing SME or a platform with hundreds of daily transactions, it becomes an operational bottleneck that no amount of "faster payments" can resolve .


### Cross-border flows add a new layer


The complexity does not stop at Tanzania's borders. in 2025,[Mobile money outflow volumes rose 13.77%](https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/tanzania/business/cross-border-mobile-money-inflows-rise-33-percent-to-sh698-billion-5488722) but value fell 19.17%, suggesting smaller, more frequent transactions .


For businesses processing these flows, a higher number of lower-value transactions can create more reconciliation records and counterparties to track.


And with Tanzania planning to[interlink TIPS with Rwanda's RSwitch](https://www.eac.int/eadrip-news-updates/eardrip-press-releases/3558-eac-intensifies-efforts-towards-a-regional-instant-payment-network-as-rwanda-and-tanzania-deepen-development-of-cross-border-payment-integration-framework) under the EAC Cross-Border Payment System Masterplan, the number of variables is only going to increase .

## 5 Things a Business Payment Provider in Tanzania should Solve


### 1. Multiple payment channels


A growing company should not have to maintain a completely separate operating process for every payment method.


### 2. Reconciliation


Collections, fees, refunds, payouts and settlements need to match the company's own transaction records.


### 3. High-volume payouts


The system should be able to process supplier, merchant or customer payments without depending on one-by-one manual transfers.


### 4. Failed transaction management


Businesses need clear payment statuses and processes for failures, reversals and retries.


### 5. Treasury and liquidity visibility


A business needs to know which funds are available, pending or restricted before committing to additional payouts.


### What Businesses Actually Need


The Bank of Tanzania's recent payment-system work increasingly emphasizes integration and interoperability alongside broader access.


In practice, this means collections and disbursements are becoming complex because the bar has been raised. A business that once needed only a mobile money number now needs a system that can:


- **Identify** who paid, for what, and through which channel
- **Reconcile** automatically across wallets, banks, and cards
- **Disburse** to suppliers, agents, and refund recipients without manual processing
- **Report** in a way that satisfies finance teams, auditors, and regulators

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best payment gateway for businesses in Tanzania?


The right payment gateway depends on the business model and required payment channels. Businesses processing high volumes should also consider payout support, reconciliation, APIs, transaction reporting and settlement visibility rather than choosing only on collection capability.


### What payment methods are commonly used in Tanzania?


Mobile money is a major part of Tanzania's payment ecosystem, alongside banks and cards. The country also operates TIPS for interoperable instant payments between participating providers.


### Can businesses automate payouts in Tanzania?


Yes. Payout APIs and business payment infrastructure can be used to automate payments to suppliers, merchants, customers, agents and other beneficiaries.


### What are Accruals and Disbursements?


Accruals and Disbursements refer to the infrastructure businesses use to manage incoming and outgoing money. Accruals cover funds collected or accumulated by the business, while disbursements cover money sent to suppliers, merchants, customers, employees or other beneficiaries. Miden combines these flows with reconciliation, transaction reporting and payment controls.


### Why do businesses need automated reconciliation?


When a company handles thousands of collections and payouts, manual matching becomes slow and more prone to errors. Automated reconciliation helps connect payment records with the corresponding transaction and settlement information.


### What is the difference between pay-ins and payouts?


A pay-in is money entering the business, usually from a customer or partner. A payout is money the business sends to another party, such as a supplier, employee, merchant or customer.
